neighbours.label: a clause-opening adverb that introduces an earlier state ('Originally', 'Previously', 'Initially', 'At first') after a preceding sentence
fire: The site now holds a shopping mall. Originally, it was a cattle market.
The rules changed in 2015. Previously, workers could retire at sixty.
The app is now free to use. Initially, it cost five dollars a month.
Today the team plays in red. Originally the club wore green shirts.
The bridge carries cars and buses. Previously it was used only by trains.
She now works as a nurse. Initially, she trained as a lawyer.
The festival lasts a full week. Originally, it was a single afternoon.
The drug treats migraines. Previously, doctors prescribed it for blood pressure.
quiet: The site now holds a shopping mall. Nearby, there is a cattle market.
The rules changed in 2015. Since then, workers can retire at sixty.
The app is now free to use. Still, it shows ads every few minutes.
Today the team plays in red. Their rivals wear green shirts.
The bridge carries cars and buses. It is also used by cyclists.
She now works as a nurse. Her brother trained as a lawyer.
The festival lasts a full week. Each day has a different theme.
The drug treats migraines. Doctors also prescribe it for blood pressure.

notes: Card top examples are mixed with periods; probe gave only ~0.1 of max on bare sentence-initial use, so fire items put the adverb after a prior sentence.
